Quick guide

1. Get the photos from the camera

  1. On the camera, move the photos to the FTP folder: the program only sees the ones in there.
  2. Turn on the camera's WiFi and FTP and connect the PC to its network (for example “termica”). The Connect button in the left panel does it for you.
  3. When it says Connected, click Get new photos: it downloads only the new photos to Thermal photos › Imported › date.

If it says the camera did not give the PC an address, click Reconnect (or disconnect and reconnect the WiFi).

2. Organize: one folder per location

Create a folder per piece of equipment or site (for example North Substation › Panel A) and drag the photos from each round into it. Comparison and trend use the folder as the “location”.

3. View and measure

  • Palette and Contrast: “Like the camera” spreads the colors to show details; “Linear” compares photos on the same scale. Temperatures do not change.
  • Auto fits the range to the image excluding the sky; the lock keeps it when switching photos.
  • Toolbar tools: point (P), line (L) with temperature profile and area (R). Esc goes back to move and select.
  • In the measurements table, mark one as Reference (★): the ΔT of the others is how much hotter they are than it. It changes the least between summer and winter, so it is the best way to detect problems.
  • Double-click the name to change it. Use the same names in every round (“Phase R”, “Phase S”…): that way they can be tracked over time.
  • The notes in the right panel are saved automatically and appear in the report.

4. Track a location over time

  • Compare (C): the open photo next to another of the same location, on the same scale, with the date in large type and measurements with the same name matched.
  • Trend (E), next to the gallery title: chart of the max and the ΔT of each measurement across all photos in the folder.

5. Report and export

  • Report (Ctrl+P): PDF with a cover page and one page per photo (thermal with measurements, visible photo, table with ΔT and notes).
  • File › Export: image with measurements (PNG), measurements or all temperatures (CSV for Excel).

Accuracy

Temperatures are calculated from each photo's radiometric data: ±%(tipico)s typical between %(lo)s and %(hi)s, compared with what the camera shows. Photos taken in the camera's high range are not calibrated yet and show a warning.
